purpose: Collects run output as per-stream prefixes with explicit loss, limit and drain semantics.
behavior: Claims the output consumer when collect is called, before its future is polled; collection budget is max+1 per stream.
Processes queued events in order so first limit/loss/read failure wins; each stream truncates to max on limit and gaps yield Io with partial prefixes.
After end(), waits on a deadline running on the library runtime; pending unreported drops still fail a bounded finish.
contracts: Dropping even an unpolled collection future permanently detaches its claim.
dependencies: io/queue Shared supplies ordered events and budgets; process/run.rs stops trees and attaches results.
failures_or_limits: Text conversion uses UTF-8 replacement; byte mode preserves captured bytes.

purpose: Connects source pipes or terminal output to pumps, single-consumer views, collection and stdin.
behavior: Starts one reader per existing source; terminal output is labeled Pty in stdout slot.
Claiming output or lines reserves the sole consumer; dropped counters are per stream and collect claims synchronously.
end starts a one-second drain deadline, while dropping pumps cuts immediately; Stdin wraps an independent writer thread and abandons on drop.
contracts: Pipe backpressure is explicitly enabled before claim and released by end or detach.
dependencies: io/queue, out, collect and stdin own mechanics; process/pty modules are callers.
failures_or_limits: Introductory unconditional no-loss wording must be read with the actual bounded-drop policy and backpressure exception. A blocked external pipe holder may keep a reader thread until its next wake.

purpose: Provides chunk and line consumer views with per-stream UTF-8 continuity and exact drop accounting.
behavior: Output retains incomplete UTF-8 across adjacent chunks, flushes replacement characters at gaps/end, and reports lost_before on the next stream item or final empty item.
Lines strips LF and optional preceding CR, preserves bare CR, emits final unterminated lines and breaks long text into at most 1 MiB UTF-8-safe pieces marked continues.
Dropping a view credits buffered unpublished bytes, partial lines and decoder tails to dropped totals.
contracts: Views consume the same permanent single claim; no data may be stitched across a reported gap.
dependencies: io/queue supplies ordered per-stream events and wake notifications.
failures_or_limits: Invalid UTF-8 is replacement-decoded in text and lines; byte Output is required for lossless raw content.

purpose: Maintains bounded per-stream output queues, loss ledgers and optional attached-reader backpressure.
behavior: Budgets are 1 MiB before claim, 16 MiB attached, max+1 collecting, and zero detached; adjacent same-stream chunks coalesce up to 64 KiB.
Overflow counts dropped bytes and attaches gap counts to the next event; permanent detach counts queued and consumer-held bytes and releases blocked readers.
Backpressure waits only for an attached consumer before tree end; end/cut/detach release it. cut injects EOF markers including pending loss for active views.
contracts: A second claim is InvalidArgument; root/process completion may observe ended independently of consumer drain.
dependencies: queue/reader.rs feeds Shared; out.rs consumes one event at a time; collect.rs drains batches.
failures_or_limits: The module introduction predates optional hold behavior; implementation deliberately blocks readers when hold is active.

purpose: Runs one blocking OS reader thread per output source and feeds bounded Shared state.
behavior: Creates a small-stack named reader and allocates a 64 KiB buffer on heap; terminal start waits for the worker startup signal.
Retries Interrupted reads, emits EOF on zero bytes and maps Unix PTY EIO to EOF; other read errors become stream-specific Io.
contracts: PTY startup synchronization precedes held-root Go to address immediate-exit output loss.
dependencies: io/queue Shared accepts bytes and records finish; process startup performs Go after pump startup.
failures_or_limits: Blocking reads finish only when the OS wakes them; the startup signal precedes the pump call, not a confirmed completed OS read.

purpose: Serializes stdin writes on a dedicated blocking thread with asynchronous completion replies.
behavior: Queues copied byte buffers under a mutex and completes each oneshot after write_all; close waits behind earlier queued writes before closing the handle.
abandon immediately fails current and queued writes with Closed and makes later writes fail; queued closes succeed idempotently.
BrokenPipe becomes Closed; another I/O failure becomes Io for that write and closes future admission.
contracts: Thread writes never interleave; the first shutdown reason is retained.
dependencies: io/mod.rs owns the Stdin wrapper; oneshot replies bridge the worker to any caller executor.
failures_or_limits: An OS write cannot be interrupted here: abandonment settles futures but worker exits only when the write returns. Concurrent unawaited writes can accumulate copied buffers.
inference: Bounded memory is strongest when callers await write backpressure instead of queueing many concurrent writes.
